scope: Engine-light live tuning: tunable identity, a closed set of tunable kinds (float, integer, bool, enumerated, colour, vector2, vector3), an immutable registry built by explicit registration, tuning intents (set, reset one, reset all, snapshot, apply snapshot, export) applied to an immutable tuning state whose overrides are the only diff from defaults, deterministic replay, and a token bridge that turns the shared design-language token document into a registry and a state's overrides back into a token-override document, with a thin Unity adapter planned separately that binds tunables to skin assets and other ScriptableObjects through explicit binding records, applies accepted overrides live through each renderer adapter's existing skin seam, exports through an injectable sink (a device-side JSON override file and an Editor-side asset writer), and hosts a tuning panel as a client of the XR UI shell
review_note: The URLs below were not fetched from the authoring environment because its network egress policy blocks them; the admitted claims come from the author's prior reading of these documents and must be confirmed by a person, together with the exact page paths, version pins, licenses, and open-source maintenance state, before the admission record is signed.

context_only_not_derivation_inputs.reason: The shared design-language token document is the primary input the token bridge reads and the primary output the Editor writer writes back to; it is the thing being tuned, not a derivation input for the tuning model

The Inventory renderer adapters' skin seams (InventoryUiToolkitSkin and InventorySkin) are the first ScriptableObjects that binding records target and the entry points through which accepted overrides are applied live; their code, samples, and evidence are neither derivation inputs nor transferable evidence for this family

The tuning panel is a client of the XR UI shell for placement, anchoring, routing, and the shell skin; the shell's layout and routing model is not re-derived here, and the interim UGUI fallback exists only until the shell's UGUI adapter is live

The Settings family owns player-facing typed settings, profiles, transactions, applicators, and persistence; live tuning is a developer-facing tool with no profiles, scopes, or transactions and must never ship to players. A Settings definition may be exposed as a tunable only through an explicit bridge that forwards accepted set intents as Settings intents, which is a later proposal, not part of this gate

source_gate_non_claims: No source grants package maturity, release, certification, platform review outcome, or device authority

The first implementation is a tunable-identity, registry, intent, immutable-state, and token-bridge substrate with a thin binding, export, and panel adapter; it is not a runtime settings menu for players, not a profiler, and not an inspector of arbitrary objects

The family guarantees the plumbing only: that an accepted override reached the bound skin seam and that an export wrote the override document it reports; whether a value looks right in the headset is a human judgement recorded in a Device Lab receipt
Legibility, contrast, comfort, latency, and any headset, controller, or input behaviour are device claims that require a Device Lab receipt, never an EditMode result or a source citation
Automated or device evidence recorded for one renderer adapter's skin seam never transfers to the other renderer adapter or its composition
